title: Determination of short-chain chlorinated paraffins in multiple matrices of Arctic using gas chromatography-electron capture negative ion-low resolution mass spectrometry
author: Li, Fu, et al.
materials: The commercial standards of the SCCPs (chlorine contents of 51.5%, 55.5%, and 63.0%, with the congener group patterns shown in Fig. 1) at concentrations of 100 ng/μL in cyclohexane and ε-hexachlorocyclohexane (ε-HCH, solution in cyclohexane, 10 ng/μL) were purchased from Ehrenstorfer GmbH (Augsburg, Germany). The 13C10-trans-chlordane (100 ng/μL solution in n-nonane, purity 99%) was purchased from Cambridge Isotope Laboratories (Andover, USA). Pesticide-grade dichloromethane, n-hexane, acetone, cyclohexane, and toluene were purchased from JT Baker (Phillipsburg, NJ). Florisil (60–100 mesh) and silica gel (180–280 mesh) were purchased from Merck (Whitehouse Station, NJ). Anhydrous sodium sulfate was purchased from Sinopharm Chemical Reagent Beijing Co., Ltd.Fig. 1Congener group pattern for commercial references of SCCPs (C10-13, 51.5%, 55.5% and 63.0% chlorine content).Fig. 1

Silica gel was activated at 550 °C for 12 h, Florisil was activated at 140 °C for 7 h, and anhydrous sodium sulfate was activated at 660 °C for 6 h before use. A mixture of 30% (40%) acid silica gel was prepared by mixing 100 g of activated silica gel and 44 g (66 g) of concentrated sulfuric acid.

steps.title: Activate sorbents and prepare acid silica
steps.instruction: Activate silica gel at 550 °C for 12 h, Florisil at 140 °C for 7 h, and anhydrous sodium sulfate at 660 °C for 6 h. Prepare 30 % (and 40 %) acid silica gel by mixing 100 g activated silica gel with 44 g (for 30 %) or 66 g (for 40 %) concentrated H₂SO₄.

steps.title: Prepare glassware for analysis
steps.instruction: Soak all glassware in deionized water containing neutral Decon 90 for >6 h, wash ≥6 times with tap water, then 3 times with deionized water. Heat in a muffle furnace at 450 °C, cool, and rinse twice with dichloromethane before use.

steps.title: Spike samples and perform ASE extraction
steps.instruction: Weigh ~5 g soil/sediment or 2 g biota, spike each with 1 ng ¹³C₁₀‑trans‑chlordane, add 15 g anhydrous sodium sulfate, and extract with dichloromethane/hexane (1:1, v/v) using a Dionex ASE 350 at 100 °C, 1500 psi, 10 min equilibration, three static cycles, and a 120 s N₂ purge.

steps.title: Remove interferences and filter extracts
steps.instruction: For soil/sediment extracts, add activated copper granules to remove elemental sulfur. For biota extracts, add 40 % acid silica gel (w/w) to remove lipids, then filter through ~5 g anhydrous sodium sulfate.

steps.title: Column cleanup and fraction collection
steps.instruction: Rotary‑evaporate each extract to ~2 mL, then pass it through a multilayer column (bottom→top: 3 g Florisil, 2 g activated silica gel, 5 g 30 % acid silica gel, 4 g anhydrous sodium sulfate). Pre‑clean the column with 50 mL hexane. Elute sequentially with 40 mL hexane (first fraction) and 100 mL dichloromethane/hexane (1:1, v/v) (second fraction).

steps.title: Concentrate extract and add internal standard
steps.instruction: Concentrate the second fraction, exchange solvent to cyclohexane and bring to a final volume of 100 µL. Add 10 ng ε‑HCH internal standard before instrumental analysis.

steps.title: GC‑ECNI‑MS instrumental analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 1 µL of the final extract splitless into a 7890 A GC equipped with a DB‑5MS column (30 m × 0.25 mm i.d., 0.25 µm film) at 275 °C. Use He carrier gas at 1.0 mL min⁻¹. Oven program: 1 min at 100 °C, ramp to 160 °C at 30 °C min⁻¹ (hold 5 min), ramp to 310 °C at 30 °C min⁻¹ (hold 17 min). MS: ECNI mode with methane reagent gas, transfer line 275 °C, ion source 200 °C, low‑resolution single quad. Quantify with the most abundant isotope, identify with the second most abundant. Analyze SCCP congeners in four groups (C10, C11, C12, C13) via four separate injections.

steps.title: Identify and quantify SCCP congeners
steps.instruction: Identify congener groups by matching retention time, signal shape, and isotope ratio (per Reth et al.). Correct SIM signals of [M‑Cl]⁻ ions for isotopic abundance and response factors, then calculate relative integrated signals. Use three commercial SCCP standards (51.5 %, 55.5 %, 63.0 % Cl) and prepared mixtures (e.g., 51.5 %/55.5 % = 53 %; 55.5 %/63 % = 59.5 %; etc.) to build calibration curves; a linear correlation (R² = 0.96) between chlorine content and total response factor is obtained.

steps.title: Quality assurance and control procedures
steps.instruction: Pre‑wash all sample equipment with hexane and dichloromethane before Arctic transport. Dry, homogenize, pack samples in aluminium foil, seal in clean bags, and store at –20 °C. Use anhydrous sodium sulfate as a blank throughout sampling, transport, storage, drying, homogenizing, extraction, cleanup, and analysis (blank concentrations 0.56–2.17 ng g⁻¹, <5 % of average sample 165.2 ng g⁻¹). Process procedural blanks for each batch (LOD ≈ 0.1 ng). Verify recoveries: ¹³C₁₀‑trans‑chlordane 66–96 %; spiked SCCP standards 81–116 %. Validate accuracy with three replicate analyses of an Arctic moss sample (232.4, 289.1, 268.6 ng g⁻¹ dw) and duplicate measurements.
